pll1d39c4-d1e3501.summary: Raises Jerome's objection on Habakkuk: it is absurd to say God knows moment by moment how many gnats or fish are born and die, or that he has the same providence for irrational and rational creatures. This seems to deny God's knowledge or providence of the least things, and so that he knows all at once and always.

pll1d39c4-d1e3526.summary: Explains that Jerome denies only that God knows these alternately or moment by moment, as they arise and perish, or provides for them as for rational creatures ('does God care for oxen?'). Yet Scripture says God cares for all; he has universal providence over all he made, giving each its due, but special providence for rational creatures, to whom he gave precepts, law, rewards, and guardian angels. So God knows the number of gnats and fish, not moment by moment but simultaneously and always.
claims: God knows all things simultaneously, not moment by moment.
God has general providence over all creatures.
God has special providence for rational creatures.

pll1d39c4-d1e3581.summary: Concludes that God knows simultaneously and immutably all that was, is, and will be, good and evil, and foreknows all future things, good and evil.
claims: God knows all things simultaneously and immutably.

pl-l1d39c4.summary: Faces Jerome's statement on Habakkuk that it is absurd to say God knows moment by moment how many gnats are born or die, or that his providence is the same for irrational and rational creatures. Lombard reads Jerome as denying only that God knows such things successively, moment by moment, or provides for irrational creatures as for rational ones. God has universal providence and care for all he made, so each has what it is due; but he has special providence for rational creatures, to whom he gave precepts, law, rewards, and guardian angels, which is the sense of 'does God care for oxen?' So God knows the number of gnats and fish, simultaneously and always, and knows and foreknows all past, present, and future, good and evil, immutably.
claims: Jerome denies only that God knows creatures moment by moment or provides for all alike.
God knows all things, even the smallest, simultaneously and always.
God has general providence over all creatures.
God has special providence for rational creatures, with precepts, rewards, and angels.
God knows and foreknows all things, good and evil, immutably.
